title: A vendor invoice goes to QuickBooks as a bill with its stored due date
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the test organization is connected to a QuickBooks Online sandbox company, and you can sign in to that company in another tab.
  • Make sure vendor A holds the shop's own term A, due 14 days after the invoice date, not yet in QuickBooks; a vendor invoice A for it, dated Oct 5, 2026, is stored due Oct 19, 2026 and not yet sent.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Send vendor invoice A to QuickBooks the way the shop does today.
  2. In QuickBooks, open the bill.
  3. In QuickBooks, open the Terms list (Settings, All lists, Terms).
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • It is sent.

Step 2:

  • It is a bill for vendor A, due Oct 19, 2026, with terms term A.

Step 3:

  • Term A was created, as a standard term due in 14 days.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11677 (Story 8, QuickBooks sync - credit terms)

  • S8-R5: “Each invoice carries its own term and due date to QuickBooks, as today. A vendor invoice is sent to QuickBooks as a bill with its stored due date (S7-R9) and the vendor's term at the moment it is sent.”
  • S8-R1: “When a record is sent to QuickBooks with a term QuickBooks does not have, ShopView first creates the term in QuickBooks under the same name, then sends the record. This is how the standard terms already work today.”
  • S8-R2: “A "Due Net X days" term is created in QuickBooks as a standard term due in X days.”
  • Terminology: “Vendor invoice → The app's word for a bill received from a vendor. QuickBooks calls the same record a bill; this PRD says "bill" only when describing what appears inside QuickBooks.”
